decision: Open a relay/endpoint design slice before R1f. The unchanged recipe has no observed UDP source-learning path to the game service; advertising selfreported ports alone fails on the measured two-port-changing path. Do not implement endpoint learning as a confirmed fix.

reuse.source: CP261 retained ARM baseline/client4b/native account recipe and observers; CP264 scoped acceptance; CP265 R1e merged PR344
reuse.direct: Retain server/client/config/fixture/body99/153/native send/getter/ingress and lifecycle recipes. Only B NAT and second-run cloud observation exception differ.
reuse.method_only: Previous positive verifier parser/reassembly and post-run ACL/routing/raw/quiescence checks. Negative assertions are separate and not a weakened positive test.
reuse.must_measure: Both selfreported-vs-postNAT ports in same run, native destination/ingress and UDP seen by service; R2 supplies R1 missing ApostNAT capture.
reuse.avoided: No codec/account/room/battle reimplementation, no broadSDK/static scan, no repeats of one-side-reachable N1 positives as new gate claims.

limits: N1b is a completed bounded architecture measurement with a negative directUDP result, not a passed two-NAT gameplay gate or implemented relay.
Current finite native send/ingress windows and full named captures show no UDP arriving at the service; this is not proof that every KR mode/protocol lacks NAT traversal.
Same CP261 retained ARM service/admin and copy4b/Wine; no runtime source/config/input changed during either run. Current R1e binary is not natively certified by these runs.

B is controlled port-changing NAT; two roles share a physical host and B uplink uses an encapsulated carrier. Only the peer leg measured traverses real Internet. Not two independent householdISPs, all NAT classes, or CGNAT type certification.

R1cloud filter hides ApostNAT; R2 restricts the cloud observation exception to the already-allowlisted peer and reported destination port, with no Linux public DNAT. Both run raw/results are retained separately.
Actual VPS/OCI endpoints, IDs, topology, policies, routes, ranges and access details stay local. Public metadata includes only evidence hashes and bounded conclusions.
CP264 N1 one-side-reachable acceptance and CP212 K6c/K7 simulatedWAN remain unchanged. M5 generalprofiles/nativeDBqueuefault, R1f sharedNAT and finalR1native remain open.
